title: CHAPTER II. Matthew Cuthbert is surprised

paragraphs.en: Matthew Cuthbert and his sorrel mare traveled eight miles to Bright River. The road was pleasant, lined with farms and occasional patches of fir trees or hollows with wild plums. The air smelled sweet from apple orchards, and distant meadows blurred into misty horizons.
paragraphs.zh: 马修·库特伯和他那匹栗色母马驱车走了八英里，来到明亮河镇。沿途的路景宜人，两旁是农舍，偶尔可见一片片云杉或是长满野生李子树的小洼地。空气中弥漫着苹果园散发出的甜美香气，远处的草地在晨雾中渐渐模糊成一片朦胧的天际线。

paragraphs.en: Matthew enjoyed the ride but avoided women, nodding to them out of obligation rather than choice. He feared they secretly mocked his appearance: an awkward figure with long gray hair reaching his shoulders and a full brown beard that had been there since he was twenty. His youthful and old age seemed indistinguishable except for a lack of graying.
paragraphs.zh: 马修喜欢骑马，但对女性避而远之，只是出于礼貌向她们点头致意，并非出自自愿。他害怕她们暗中嘲笑他的模样：一个动作笨拙、留着及肩灰发和浓密棕色胡须的男子，自二十岁起就没有变过样。他的青春与暮年似乎并无二致，唯一的区别就是没有白发。

paragraphs.en: At Bright River, Matthew found no train. Believing he arrived too early, he tethered his horse at the small hotel and approached the station house. Ignoring the girl sitting on shingles, he hurried past without looking.
paragraphs.zh: 在Bright River，马修没有等到火车。他认为自己来得太早，便把马拴在小旅店旁，匆匆走向车站。他没理会坐在木板上的女孩，径直走了过去。

paragraphs.en: She sat stiffly, clearly waiting for something or someone, her posture tense with anticipation.
paragraphs.zh: 她坐得笔直，显然在等待着什么或某人，姿势紧张而充满期待。

paragraphs.en: Matthew spoke to the stationmaster about the five-thirty train, who was just locking up to go home for supper.
paragraphs.zh: 马修和车站站长交谈着五点半的那班火车，站长刚刚锁上门准备回家吃晚饭。

paragraphs.en: Matthew Cuthbert received a surprise when the stationmaster informed him that Mrs. Alexander Spencer had brought a girl for adoption from an orphan asylum. He expected to adopt a boy, as arranged with Mrs. Spencer. The stationmaster suggested Matthew should question the girl himself.
paragraphs.zh: 马修·库伯特收到站长的通知后大吃一惊，原来亚历山大·斯宾塞太太从孤儿院带来了一个女孩来领养。他原本计划收养一个男孩，并且已经与斯宾塞太太商量好了此事。站长建议马修最好亲自去问一下这个女孩。

paragraphs.en: "Guess there's some mistake," he said. "Mrs. Spencer came off the train with the girl and gave her into my charge."
paragraphs.zh: “恐怕搞错了，”他说，“斯宾塞太太从火车上下来带着那个女孩，把人交给了我。”

paragraphs.en: Matthew felt helpless, wishing Marilla were present to handle the situation. He walked towards the girl, who had been watching him. She was about eleven years old, dressed in a short, tight, and ugly yellowish-gray dress.
paragraphs.zh: 马修感到束手无策，希望玛丽拉在场能处理这种情况。他走向那个正盯着他的女孩。她大约十一岁，穿着一件短小紧身且颇为难看的浅黄色衣服。

paragraphs.en: Her hair was thick and red, tied back in two braids. Her face was small, white, thin, and freckled, with large green or gray eyes.
paragraphs.zh: 她的头发浓密呈红色，扎成了两条辫子。脸庞小巧，肤色白皙而略显瘦削，布满了红褐色的雀斑，一双眼睛或绿或灰，格外明亮。

paragraphs.en: Matthew sighed as he approached her, knowing the task would be difficult.
paragraphs.zh: 马修走近她时叹了口气，他知道这项任务将会十分棘手。

paragraphs.en: Matthew Cuthbert was surprised when a woman-child approached him, her pointed chin and bright eyes catching his attention. She held out one hand, clutching an old carpet-bag with the other.
paragraphs.zh: 马修·库伯特没想到一个女孩会走近他，她那尖尖的下巴和明亮的眼睛吸引了他的注意。她伸出一只手，另一只手紧紧攥着一个旧手提包。

paragraphs.en: "Are you Mr. Matthew Cuthbert of Green Gables?" she asked in a clear voice. "I'm glad to see you.
paragraphs.zh: “您是绿山墙农庄的马修·库奇伯特先生吗？”她声音清晰地问道，“很高兴见到您。”

paragraphs.en: I was worried you might not come."
paragraphs.zh: 我担心你可能不会来了。

paragraphs.en: She explained that if he didn't arrive, she would climb into a wild cherry tree by the bend and sleep there for the night. She imagined it would be lovely under the moonlight.
paragraphs.zh: 她解释说，如果他不出现，她会爬到弯道旁那棵野生樱桃树上，在那里过夜睡觉。她想象着在月光下入睡该是多么美妙。

paragraphs.en: Matthew awkwardly took her hand and decided to take her home without revealing any mistakes. He couldn’t leave her at Bright River, so they walked towards his horse in the yard.
paragraphs.zh: 马修局促地握了握她的手，决定不透露任何破绽就将她送回家。他不能让她独自留在明亮河畔，于是两人向院子里的马厩走去。

paragraphs.en: The child spoke cheerfully about carrying a heavy carpet-bag. "It isn't heavy; it's full of my worldly goods but light enough for me to handle. The handle pulls out if not carried correctly, so I must keep it."
paragraphs.zh: 孩子愉快地说道：“这包并不重，里面装满了我的家当，但对我来说轻得可以提着走。如果不正确地拿着，把手会自动弹出来，所以我必须小心。”

paragraphs.en: She explained that the bag was very old and she knew how to manage it precisely.
paragraphs.zh: 她解释说，这个包非常旧了，她知道该怎么妥善处理。

paragraphs.en: They had to drive eight miles, as Mrs. Spencer had said. The child was excited about this journey, loving the prospect of driving. "I've never belonged anywhere truly," she admitted, adding that the asylum had been her worst experience despite only being there for four months.
paragraphs.zh: 她们不得不驱车八英里，正如斯宾塞太太所说。孩子对这次旅程兴奋不已，尤其喜欢驾车的感觉。“我从未真正属于任何地方，”她承认道，并补充说尽管只在那里待了四个月，精神病院却是她最糟糕的经历。

paragraphs.en: She felt Mrs. Spencer misunderstood her when she spoke openly about it.
paragraphs.zh: 她觉得斯宾塞太太误解了她，当她说起这件事时并没有藏着掖着。

paragraphs.en: The child reminisced about imagining stories in the asylum, particularly about a girl next to her who might be the daughter of an earl, stolen by a cruel nurse. "I used to lie awake at night," she said, explaining why she was so thin and wished she were plump with dimples.
paragraphs.zh: 孩子回忆起在疯人院想象的故事，特别是关于一个可能出身贵族的女孩，她曾被狠心的女仆拐走。“我常常整晚辗转反侧地想着这些事，”她说，解释自己为何如此瘦弱，希望自己能胖一些，脸上有酒窝。

paragraphs.en: They reached the buggy, and as they left the village, the child broke off a branch from a wild plum tree. "Isn't that beautiful?" she asked, looking up at the white lacy branches above them.
paragraphs.zh: 他们上了马车，当离开村庄时，孩子从一棵野生李树上折下一根枝条。“这不是很好看吗？”她抬头看着头顶那雪白而细腻的树枝，问道。

paragraphs.en: Matthew responded, "Well now, I dunno."
paragraphs.zh: 马修回答道：“嗯，现在我可说不准。”

paragraphs.en: Matthew Cuthbert was surprised by the news of a bride arriving in white with a veil. He had never seen such a sight and couldn’t imagine her appearance. However, he didn’t expect to marry himself; his homeliness made him believe no one would want him except perhaps a foreign missionary.
paragraphs.zh: 马修·库奇伯特听到有新娘穿着白色婚纱，戴着面纱到来的消息时大感意外。他从未见过这样的景象，也猜不出她的模样。不过，他压根没想到自己会娶妻；他的相貌平平让他相信，除了或许某个外国传教士外，没人会对上他的眼。

paragraphs.en: Lucy, on the other hand, dreamed of owning a white dress as her ultimate happiness. She felt ashamed wearing an old wincey dress from the asylum and imagined herself in beautiful clothes—blue silk, a big hat with flowers, and shiny accessories. Her journey to the Island was filled with joy despite feeling seasick.
paragraphs.zh: 另一方面，露西梦想拥有一件白色连衣裙作为她最大的幸福。她为自己穿着来自收容所的旧棉布衣服感到羞愧，并想象自己身着华美的服饰——蓝色丝绸、大大的花帽和闪亮的配饰。尽管晕船让她心情不佳，但她的岛行之旅依然充满了欢乐。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Spencer, who usually got seasick, stayed alert to ensure Lucy didn’t fall overboard. Lucy’s constant questions about the red roads amused Mrs. Spencer, but she couldn’t help answering them. The red roads turned out to be from wild cherry trees in bloom, much to Lucy's delight.
paragraphs.zh: 斯宾塞太太虽然通常晕船，这回却精神高度集中，以防露西掉进海里。露西不断询问那些红色道路的问题让斯宾塞太太觉得颇为好笑，但她还是忍不住回答了。原来那些红色的道路是盛开的山 cherry 树所致，这让露西欣喜不已。

paragraphs.en: Matthew was surprised by his own enjoyment. Like most quiet individuals, he appreciated the company of talkative people who let him remain silent. He had never anticipated enjoying a little girl's chatter.
paragraphs.zh: 马修对自己的享受感到意外。像大多数安静的人一样，他欣赏那些爱说话却让他保持沉默的同伴。他从未料到会喜欢一个小女孩喋喋不休的聊天。

paragraphs.en: Women were bad enough, but little girls were worse with their sidelong glances and timid approaches. This freckled girl was different; though it taxed his slower intelligence to keep up, he found her conversation engaging.
paragraphs.zh: 女人还罢了，但小孩子更让人头疼，她们那种斜着眼睛看人和羞怯的靠近方式实在令人不悦。这个满脸雀斑的小姑娘却与众不同；尽管他的思维不够敏捷，跟上她的谈话还是觉得挺有趣的。

paragraphs.en: "Go ahead and talk as much as you like," Matthew said shyly.
paragraphs.zh: “你爱说就说吧，”马修害羞地说道。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I'm so glad! We're going to get along splendidly. It's such a relief not to be told that children should be seen and not heard.
paragraphs.zh: “哦，真是太好了！我们一定能相处得很融洽。终于不用听到‘孩子嘴上要严实些’这种话了。”

paragraphs.en: People laugh at me for using big words, but if you have big ideas, you need big words to express them, right?"
paragraphs.zh: 人们嘲笑我用词太多，但如果你有宏大的想法，不就需要用更多的词汇来表达吗？

paragraphs.en: "That seems reasonable," Matthew agreed.
paragraphs.zh: “这倒也是个合理的说法,”马修赞同道。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Spencer mentioned Green Gables had trees around it, which delighted the narrator immensely. The asylum where she was staying only had a few poor, small trees in front, looking like orphans themselves.
paragraphs.zh: 斯宾塞太太提到绿山墙周围有树木，这让叙述者欣喜不已。她住的疗养院前只有几棵瘦弱的小树，看上去就像是孤儿一般。

paragraphs.en: "Is there a brook near Green Gables?" the narrator asked Matthew, forgetting to ask Mrs. Spencer earlier.
paragraphs.zh: “绿山墙附近有溪流吗？”叙述者问马修，早先他忘记去问斯宾塞太太了。

paragraphs.en: "Yes, right below the house," Matthew replied.
paragraphs.zh: “就在房子下面，”马修回答道。

paragraphs.en: The narrator expressed her long-held dream of living by a brook and wondered if dreams often come true. She felt almost perfectly happy now.
paragraphs.zh: 叙述者表达了她长久以来住在溪边的梦想，并疑惑是否梦想常常能够成真。此刻，她几乎感到无比幸福。

paragraphs.en: Matthew noticed one of the girl's long braids and said it was red. She sighed deeply, as if releasing all her sorrows with that single exhalation.
paragraphs.zh: 马修注意到其中一个女孩的长辫子，说它是红色的。她深深地叹了口气，仿佛随着这一声叹息释放了所有的忧愁。

paragraphs.en: Matthew Cuthbert listened as the girl spoke about her red hair, which she found impossible to imagine away. "Yes, it's red," she said with resignation. "It breaks my heart and will be my lifelong sorrow."
paragraphs.zh: 马修·库特伯尔听着女孩讲述她那红色头发的事，这种颜色让她难以想象没有它会是什么样子。“是的，它是红色的，”她叹了口气说，“这让我心碎，将成为我一生的遗憾。”

paragraphs.en: Matthew felt a twinge of sympathy but was also slightly dazed by the conversation. He recalled his own youthful naivety when he had been enticed on a merry-go-round at a picnic.
paragraphs.zh: 马修心中泛起一丝同情，但对话内容也让他有些晕头转向。他回想起了自己年轻时的天真，那时他曾被邀请在野餐会上坐上旋转木马。

paragraphs.en: The girl then asked Matthew if he could imagine being divinely beautiful, dazzlingly clever, or angelically good. "Well now, I—I don't know exactly," Matthew confessed honestly.
paragraphs.zh: 女孩接着问马修，他能否想象自己是天仙般美丽、聪明绝顶或是天使般善良。“嗯，我——我真的说不上来。”马修诚实地承认道。

paragraphs.en: They continued down the road until they reached the "Avenue." This stretch of four to five hundred yards was completely covered by wide-spreading apple trees, their branches heavy with white blossoms. The air below was filled with a purple twilight, and ahead, a glimpse of sunset painted the sky like a rose window at the end of a cathedral aisle.
paragraphs.zh: 他们沿着道路前行，直到到达了“大道”。这段四五百码长的路两旁栽满了枝繁叶茂的苹果树，树上开满了洁白的花朵，花枝低垂。路下的空气中弥漫着紫色的暮霭，而前方，则是夕阳余晖映红了天空，仿佛教堂过道尽头的一扇玫瑰窗。

paragraphs.en: The child remained silent throughout the journey, her thin hands clasped in front of her as she gazed up at the white splendor above. Even as they drove down the long slope to Newbridge, she never spoke or moved.
paragraphs.zh: 孩子在整个旅程中都保持着沉默，她那瘦小的手交叉在身前，仰望着头顶那片洁白的光辉。即使马车驶下长长的山坡抵达新桥镇，她也没有说过一句话，也没有动过一下。

paragraphs.en: Matthew Cuthbert noticed her silence and ventured, "I guess you're feeling pretty tired and hungry. But we haven't very far to go now—only another mile."
paragraphs.zh: 马修·库奇伯特注意到她沉默不语，试探着说道：“我想你一定感到挺累、挺饿的。不过我们现在快到了——只剩下一里路了。”

paragraphs.en: She finally broke her reverie with a deep sigh, looking at him dreamily. "Mr. Cuthbert," she whispered, "that place we came through—that white place—what was it?"
paragraphs.zh: 她终于从沉思中醒来，叹了口气，目光迷离地望着他。“库伯特先生，”她轻声说道，“我们刚经过的那个白色的地方——那是什么地方？”

paragraphs.en: After a moment's thought, Matthew replied, "Well, you must mean the Avenue. It is a kind of pretty place."
paragraphs.zh: 经过片刻思考，马修回答道：“嗯，你说的是林荫大道吧。那倒是个挺不错的地方。”

paragraphs.en: "Pretty? Oh, PRETTY doesn't seem the right word to use. Nor beautiful, either.
paragraphs.zh: “漂亮？哦，‘漂亮’似乎都不够准确。同样，美丽也不行。”

paragraphs.en: They don’t go far enough. Oh, it was wonderful—wonderful. It’s the first thing I ever saw that couldn’t be improved upon by imagination.
paragraphs.zh: 他们做得还不够。哦，真是太棒了——真的太棒了。这是我第一次看到的无法通过想象加以改进的事物。

paragraphs.en: It just satisfies me here"—she placed her hand on her breast—"it made a queer funny ache and yet it was a pleasant ache. Did you ever have an ache like that, Mr. Cuthbert?"
paragraphs.zh: “这让我感到挺舒服的——”她按了按胸口，“这种奇怪而有趣的疼痛其实还挺让人舒心。库伯特先生，你有没有试过这样的痛感？”

paragraphs.en: Matthew replied, "Well now, I just can't recollect that I ever had."
paragraphs.zh: 马修回答道：“说实在的，我真想不起来曾经有过这样的事。”

paragraphs.en: Matthew Cuthbert looked at the winding pond below them and said, "That's Barry's Pond." Anne disagreed, suggesting instead, "Let's call it the Lake of Shining Waters. It fits just right."
paragraphs.zh: 马修·库奇伯特向下指着蜿蜒的小湖，说道：“那就是巴里湖。”安妮不同意他的说法，提议道：“我们叫它闪耀之湖吧。这个名字再合适不过了。”

paragraphs.en: Anne continued her musings about names, recalling how she always imagined a new name when she didn't like the original one. She mentioned an asylum girl named Hepzibah Jenkins whom she called Rosalia DeVere in her mind.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮继续思考着名字的问题，回想起每当她不喜欢原本的名字时，总会想象一个新的名字。她提到了一个叫赫兹芭·詹金斯的精神病院女孩，并在心里给她改名叫罗莎莉亚·德韦尔。

paragraphs.en: As they approached home, Anne expressed her longing for a real home, feeling a pleasant ache at the thought of arriving there after their drive. Matthew noted that they had only another mile to go before reaching home.
paragraphs.zh: 当他们接近家的时候，安妮表达了她对真正家的渴望，想到即将结束车程回到家，心中涌起了一种愉悦的期盼。马修注意到，再有一英里路他们就能到家了。

paragraphs.en: The pond stretched out below them, its waters reflecting shifting hues of crocus, rose, and ethereal green. Above the bridge, fir and maple trees fringed the water, casting dark, translucent shadows. Wild plums leaned from the banks like white-clad girls peeking at their reflections.
paragraphs.zh: 池塘展现在他们脚下，水面映射出番红花、玫瑰和淡雅绿光的变换色彩。桥上方，云杉和枫树环绕着水面，投下深邃而透明的阴影。野生李子树像身着白衣的女孩一样斜倚在岸边，窥视着自己的倒影。

paragraphs.en: Frogs sang mournfully from the marsh at the pond's head.
paragraphs.zh: 池塘上游的沼泽中，青蛙们凄凉地鸣叫着。

paragraphs.en: A little gray house stood beyond a white apple orchard, its light shining through one of its windows as it grew darker outside.
paragraphs.zh: 一盏灯光从一扇窗户透出，照亮了这所略显灰旧的小房子。外面天色渐暗，那盏灯显得尤为明亮。

paragraphs.en: Matthew pondered.
paragraphs.zh: 马修陷入了沉思。

paragraphs.en: "Those grubs in the cucumber beds always excite me. I hate their appearance."
paragraphs.zh: “那些在黄瓜地里的小虫子总让我心烦。我讨厌看到它们。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, but Barry's pond? It can't be the same thrill," Diana said. "Grubs and a lake of shining waters—no connection there, right?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，巴里池塘？那肯定不是同样的兴奋吧？”戴安娜说，“虫子和那一片明镜般的湖水——这两者之间可没什么联系吧？”

paragraphs.en: Matthew explained, "Mr. Barry lives at Orchard Slope. From here, you'd see Green Gables if not for that big bush. But we have to go over the bridge, so it's half a mile further."
paragraphs.zh: 马修解释说：“巴里先生住在桃园坡。从这里看，如果没有那棵大树挡着，就能看到绿山墙了。不过我们要过一座桥才能过去，所以要多走半英里。”

paragraphs.en: "Does Mr. Barry have any girls? About my size," Diana wondered.
paragraphs.zh: “巴里先生有没有合适的女孩，跟我差不多大小的？”戴安娜疑惑地问道。

paragraphs.en: "He has one, eleven years old—Diana."
paragraphs.zh: “他有一个，十一岁——戴安娜。”

paragraphs.en: "Diana!" she exclaimed. "What a lovely name!"
paragraphs.zh: “戴安娜！”她脱口而出，“多美的名字啊！”

paragraphs.en: Matthew replied, "It sounds heathenish to me. I'd prefer Jane or Mary. But the schoolmaster named her that when she was born."
paragraphs.zh: 马修回答道：“听上去有点异教徒的味道。我更喜欢简或者玛丽这个名字。但那个学校老师给她取的名字就是这个。”

paragraphs.en: Diana sighed, "If only there had been such a schoolmaster for me." They reached the bridge.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜叹了口气，“要是当时有个这样的老师就好了。”她们走到了桥头。

paragraphs.en: "Almost home now," Matthew said as they drove up the hill. Diana shut her eyes tightly, afraid of the bridge's collapse. She peeked just before the middle but enjoyed the rumble.
paragraphs.zh: “快到家了，”马修边说边驾车驶上山坡。戴安娜紧闭双眼，害怕那座桥会垮塌。她刚到中间位置便偷偷看了一眼，却还是享受着那种震动的感觉。

paragraphs.en: "Isn't it wonderful to find things to like in this world?" she mused aloud.
paragraphs.zh: “在这个世界上找到值得喜欢的东西，不是很棒吗？”她出声思索着。

paragraphs.en: They arrived at Green Gables. Diana opened her eyes and said, "I'll say good night to you, dear Lake of Shining Waters."
paragraphs.zh: 她们抵达了绿山墙。戴安娜睁开了眼睛，说道：“我来和你道晚安，美丽的银湖。”

paragraphs.en: She woke up and looked around. They stood atop a hill, with the sun setting but the landscape still visible in the soft afterglow. To the west, a dark church spire stood against a marigold sky.
paragraphs.zh: 她醒来环顾四周，发现他们站在山顶上。夕阳西下，但余晖柔和，仍能看清周围的景色。西边，一座深色的教堂尖塔矗立在金黄色的天际线下。

paragraphs.en: Below was a small valley, and beyond, a gently sloping field dotted with cozy farmhouses.
paragraphs.zh: 下面是片小小的山谷，再过去是一片缓坡，点缀着几座温馨的小农舍。

paragraphs.en: Her eyes moved from one to another, eager and wistful. Finally, they rested on a house to the left, far back from the road, dimly lit by twilight trees. Above it, in the clear southwest sky, a bright white star shone like a guiding light.
paragraphs.zh: 她的眼睛在每个人脸上扫来扫去，充满期待与渴望。最终，她的目光落在左边一栋房子上，这栋房子远离道路，黄昏时分被周围的树木映得若隐若现。房子上方，西南方向的天空中挂着一颗明亮的白星，仿佛一盏指引的灯塔。

paragraphs.en: "That's it, isn't it?" she said, pointing.
paragraphs.zh: “就是它了，对吧？”她指着前方说道。

paragraphs.en: Matthew slapped the reins on the sorrel’s back happily. "Well now, you’ve guessed it! But I reckon Mrs. Spencer described it so's you could tell."
paragraphs.zh: 马修拍了拍红棕色马的背，高兴地说：“你猜对了！不过斯宾塞太太描述得挺清楚，你能猜到。”

paragraphs.en: "No, she didn’t—really she didn’t," she replied. "All she said might as well have been about most of those other places. I hadn't any real idea what it looked like.
paragraphs.zh: “不，她没有——真的没有。”她回答说，“她说的那些话和说到其他大多数地方差不多。我其实根本不知道它长什么样子。”

paragraphs.en: But just as soon as I saw it, I felt it was home. Oh, it seems as if I must be in a dream. My arm is black and blue from the elbow up; I’ve pinched myself so many times today.
paragraphs.zh: 但当我一看到它，我就觉得这就是我的家。哦，好像我正做着美梦呢。今天我已经好几次发现自己胳膊从肘部以上都青了一片，肯定是被自己无意中掐的。

paragraphs.en: Every little while, a horrible sickening feeling would come over me, and I’d be afraid it was all a dream. Then I'd pinch myself to see if it was real—until suddenly I remembered that even supposing it was only a dream, I’d better go on dreaming as long as I could; so I stopped pinching. But it is real, and we’re nearly home."
paragraphs.zh: 每隔一会儿，我都会被一种可怕的恶心感笼罩，担心这一切只是个梦。于是我会掐自己确认是否真实——直到突然想起即便这只是个梦，我也最好尽可能地继续做下去；因此我停下了掐自己的动作。但事实是，我们快到家了。

paragraphs.en: She sighed with joy and fell silent. Matthew shifted uncomfortably; he was relieved it would be Marilla who had to break the news that the child's dream home wouldn't come true. As they drove through Lynde's Hollow, now dark but still visible from Mrs. Rachel's window, up the hill, and into Green Gables' long lane, Matthew dreaded the revelation.
paragraphs.zh: 她高兴地叹了口气，随后沉默了下来。马修坐立不安；他松了口气，庆幸这次要由玛丽拉来告诉孩子，她的梦想家园恐怕无法实现这个消息。当他们驾车穿过林德谷，夜色已深但仍依稀可见雷切尔太太窗前的灯火，沿着山坡上行，驶入绿山墙那条长长的车道时，马修心中满是担忧与不安。

paragraphs.en: He worried more about the child’s disappointment than his own or Marilla's trouble.
paragraphs.zh: 他更担心孩子的失望，而不是自己或玛丽拉的麻烦。

paragraphs.en: The yard was dark as they entered, with poplar leaves whispering softly around them. She whispered, "Listen to the trees talking in their sleep; what nice dreams they must have!" Holding tightly onto her carpet-bag, containing all she owned, she followed Matthew into the house.
paragraphs.zh: 院里一片漆黑，白杨树叶轻声细语地环绕在他们周围。她低声说道：“听那树儿们在梦中低语；它们一定做了些美妙的梦吧！”紧紧攥着装有所有家当的手提包，她跟着马修走进了屋内。
